Bring snacks, water and beverages. Clean the car of any contraband as needed (not assuming anything, just a suggestion if it applies).

If your phone is equipped, Google Maps is good for showing traffic issues. Bring a charger both for wall and vehicle.

Travel light. Don't leave valuables in your vehicle. Let at least someone know your plan and schedule in case something happens, like being brutally murdered by a random clown or something.

Obey traffic laws. Bring both cash and credit/debit cards. Check/plan for tolls and bring change or w/e people use now days.

Get your car checked out, oil changed, etc. Check tires, brakes, top off fluids (and bring spare oil, washer fluid, anti-freeze, and an empty gas can.) Flashlight with good batteries. Check your spare and jack, know how to use them safely.

Just be smart by covering most exposed skin and dress warmly in layers - frostbite is not a joke. You will need to spend some money on a good winter coat, boots, warm gloves/mittens, long underwear, etc. Look for boots and parkas that are temp rated to at least -25F (yes, that's a negative 25), order them online if necessary before you need them. I'm really not trying to scare you, I just don't want you to have problems that are easily avoidable with a little preparation. It won't be -25F every day. There will be a few days of it several times, likely in January and February, but then it warms up to something more bearable. The temperature and windchill (which tells you what it feels like outside - like a reverse heat index) just tells you how much winter gear to wear. This article is kinda helpful, talking about layering: Art of Manliness layering. Unless you're working outside all day, you'll mostly be going from one heated environment to another without much outside exposure, just like you would from one air-conditioned place to another in a Texas summer.

Frostbite is mostly a concern when you're out in the cold for long periods of time, or not properly covering exposed skin when the windchill is really low. It means your skin tissue has frozen. I do a 36 hour round trip 5-6 times a year and here's what I recommend:

Car Something comfortable to drive, Cruise Control, Tinted windows (the sun is a beast), Sunglasses that won't hurt leaving on for a while, Wear gym shorts and a t-shirt while driving, Inflate your tires to the max recommended pressure for best gas mileage, Make sure your spare is aired up and you have the tools to change a tire, Rain -X the windows before you leave, Replace the windshield wipers before you leave, Wax the car (helps keep water off while driving), Service the car before you leave.

Food (pack the good stuff) Nuts for a good low fat snack, PB&J for sugar, Chips, Fruit, Water, Don't get that afternoon crash.

Other Bring a gun, know the laws in each state about keeping it loaded, Bring a small tool box for the mishaps, Bring a knife and a blunt object like a bat or something (personal protection), Know how to change a tire, Don't let the tank get below 1/4 %.

Bring a note book, make voice memos while driving and write down mile markers that are memorable when you stop like good (safe) gas stations, places to stretch your legs (I like Gander Mountain, Cabelas, Outlet Malls) and how many miles are in each state. You can figure out mileage by knowing that once you enter a state heading southbound that the mile markers are counting down, if you are heading into a state northbound they are counting up. If you are heading west the mile markers count up, east they count down. Know miles in each state and know how many miles you get to the tank to avoid that stress over gas.

And finally... enjoy the view! We live in a big beautiful country! Enjoy it!
